requiredFindings.title: Resolve the no-errno scratch-exhaustion representation explicitly
requiredFindings.detail: LD-D3A-12 correctly gives removal its own finite work budget and preserves admission on cleanup failure, but specifies supervision.scratch.retained {errno} for exhaustion with no errno. M3-D item 12 closes scratch to removed or retained(errno), item 20 requires retaining/logging the failure with its errno, and item 21 declares that event's errno field. LD-D3A-10 simultaneously promises exact required field/optionality preservation and a C-2 check rejecting missing or extra fields. Work-budget exhaustion is not a failed syscall and supplies no actual errno. As written, this path must either omit the promised required field, manufacture an errno, or construct a settlement outside the stated closed shape.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Choose and document a lawful typed representation for retained scratch caused by work-budget exhaustion, distinguishing it from retained(errno) for actual I/O failure. If that requires a narrow M3-D content/descriptor amendment, make it explicit in the lead decision and authority record rather than calling it unchanged field preservation. Align the settlement, event fields/optionality, registry descriptor check and exhaustion controls. Preserve cleanup noninterference with admission, and do not synthesize an OS errno for budget exhaustion.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Bind the fixture path to this build rather than directory uniqueness
nonBlockingObservations.detail: The harness-free executable resolves stdout contamination, but scanning the deps directory for a unique supervisor_fixture-<hash> does not identify the artifact produced by this invocation. Incremental target directories can contain several prior hashes, or only an unrelated stale artifact when a filtered test invocation did not build the fixture. Failing on ambiguity is safe but unnecessarily makes ordinary reruns brittle. Have the lane/build invocation supply or verify the exact test artifact path, require that the fixture target was built, and define a harmless no-behavior entry when Cargo runs the harness-free target on its own.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Qualify the no-child/no-scratch Drop control for disclosed ceiling failures
nonBlockingObservations.detail: D3-T3 still says Drop in each state leaves no child and no scratch, and the mutation list still treats an unsettled Drop leaving a child as invariably wrong. The new Unreaped path intentionally retains custody and may leave a surviving root at the ceiling; bounded removal may intentionally retain scratch. State that the absolute cleanup assertion applies to killable/removable fixtures, and that ceiling or work-exhaustion fixtures instead assert finite settlement, correct retained/unreaped disclosure, custody preservation and no later signal/blocking reap. The new D3a-0 controls already support this distinction.
